reason: Only the less common 'picturesque' fits well, since 'the slower beautiful route' sounds awkward without 'more' or a comma, and 'country' or 'mountain' route fit the grammar but do not mean 'có phong cảnh đẹp'.
The closest candidate, "app", does not fit because "web app" means an application that runs inside a browser, not a program like Chrome or Firefox.
The modifier 'visual' strongly favours 'clutter'; 'mess' is awkward after 'visual', and only less common options like 'chaos' or 'noise' fit, with a slightly different meaning.
The closest candidates, 'manage' and 'hope', are grammatical, but they mean succeeding or hoping, not having enough money (đủ khả năng chi trả), and 'can't pay to rent' is unnatural.
The closest candidate, "buy", needs no "for", and "ask" or "wait" fit the grammar but do not mean "trả tiền".
"Tense" (căng thẳng) fits naturally and keeps the meaning, and common words like "difficult" or "hard" also fit the contrast with "relaxing".
"Recall" fits naturally and means nhớ, but it is a more formal word that few A1 learners would write; "love" and "picture" change the meaning or sound unnatural.
The common word "stop" (and the synonym "stopover") fits naturally, as in "during our stop in Istanbul", and keeps the meaning of a connecting-flight stop.
The closest candidates, "cooking" and "food", do not fit because "haute" forms the fixed phrase "haute cuisine", and "couture" means fashion, not ẩm thực.
The closest candidate, "menu", does not fit because "order dinner from room menu" is not natural English, while "room service" is a fixed compound.
Only the close variant "encode" (also 'mã hóa') fits, while "lock" and "secure" do not mean 'mã hóa' and clash with the 'decryption key' clue.
The closest candidate, "lemon", fits "yellow ___ peel" grammatically, but it means quả chanh, not quả chuối, and slipping on a peel is the classic banana cartoon gag.
The closest candidate, "sort", breaks the fixed phrase "reduce, reuse and recycle" and does not mean "tái chế", so only "recycle" fits.
"Make" fits naturally ("make fresh bread in the oven") and is a common A1 word, so a learner who writes it would be marked wrong.
"Decorate" fits naturally ("decorate it with a sprig of parsley, mainly for colour"), keeps the meaning "trang trí", and is a common word learners know; "top" also fits.
The closest candidate, "plan" (savings plan), is less natural with "opened at the bank" and means "kế hoạch", not "tài khoản"; "book" and "deposit" also do not fit naturally.
The closest candidates are "buy" (you cannot buy your own bike), and "fix" or "rent" (natural, but they do not mean "bán"), so only "sell" fits.
The closest candidate, "bubble", is natural but only describes the gas and does not mean "lên men"; "react", "change" and "brew" are too general or unnatural here.
The closest candidate, "rice" (as in "brown rice"), does not dissolve in melted butter, and "flour" does not dissolve either, so only "sugar" fits "brown ___ until it dissolves."
Only the formal word "invoice" fits naturally; "bill" means a request for payment and "ticket" is not proof of purchase for returns.
The closest candidate, "host", usually means a hosting company rather than "máy chủ", and "page" or "site" would not be the thing that failed to handle the visitors.
Only rare or formal words such as "vie" or "contend" fit naturally with "with ... on price", while common words like "fight" or "deal" sound unnatural or change the meaning.
"Employ" fits naturally ("plans to employ three extra staff") with the same meaning and is a common word at B1 level; "recruit" also fits.
The article 'an' rules out 'virtual' and 'distance', but 'internet' or 'e-learning' could fit; these are marginal variants, as 'an internet English course' sounds dated and 'e-learning' is formal.
Common words like "push" or "upload" (and the variant "redeploy") fit naturally in "___ the previous version to the servers" with the same meaning, so a learner who writes them would be marked wrong.
The common A1 word "bag" fits naturally ("packing my clothes into a large bag with wheels"), and so does "case", so a learner who writes either would be marked wrong.

The closest candidates, 'team' and 'employees', do not fit without an article or change of structure ('a member of team' and 'a member of employees' are ungrammatical), and 'personnel' sounds unnatural here, so only 'staff' fits.
The common A1 words "use", "have" and "take" all fit naturally ("Can I use your pen for a minute? I'll give it back"), and in this context they convey borrowing.

The closest candidate, "atlas" (as in "road atlas"), is a bound book that you open rather than spread out, and other words such as "chart" or "plan" do not collocate with "road"; only "map" fits naturally.
The closest candidates are "save" and "buy": "save in government bonds" is unnatural and "buy" does not take "in", so only "invest" fits the blank.
"Display" fits and means màn hình, but it is less common than "screen" and above A1 level; "glass" and "case" change the meaning.
The common words 'raised' and 'picked up' fit naturally ('raised his speed', 'picked up his speed') and keep the meaning 'tăng', but would be marked wrong.

The closest candidate, "bargain", does not fit: the buyer accepting the offer would not say "you've got a bargain", and "agreement" clashes with the article "a", so only the fixed phrase "you've got a deal" works.
Common words such as "set up", "put" (put programs on a computer) and "add" fit naturally and keep the meaning "cài đặt", so a learner writing one of them would be marked wrong.
"Programmer" fits: "a freelance web programmer" is natural, means exactly "lập trình viên", and is a common word a B2 learner knows.
The closest candidate, "app", is a different thing from cloud storage, and "computer" or "album" either sound unnatural with "in the" or would not keep the photos safe.
"Wi-Fi" fits naturally ("the office has a Wi-Fi network"), keeps the meaning of "không dây", and is a word almost every learner knows.
"Piece" fits naturally in "a thin piece of lemon", keeps the meaning "miếng mỏng", and is a common A1 word.
The closest candidate, "lunch", does not fit because "every morning before she goes to school" points only to breakfast, and "brunch" or "snack" are not natural there.
"Neat" (and also "clean") fits naturally in "keep our bedrooms ___" with the meaning gọn gàng, and both are common words an A2 learner knows.
The closest candidate, "allergen", forms a natural phrase with "list" but means "chất gây dị ứng", not "nguyên liệu", and "food list" and "contents list" are not natural on a label.
"Yearly" keeps the meaning, but "yearly general meeting" is an unusual variant of the fixed term "annual general meeting"; "next" fits the grammar but loses the meaning "hằng năm".
Only less natural options fit, such as the redundant "washing" service or the formal "valet" service; "cleaning" service suggests room cleaning, not đồ giặt.
"Bags" fits naturally ("left all our bags at the left luggage office") and is a common A1 word meaning luggage; "baggage" and "things" also fit.

"Well-paid" (or "profitable") fits the blank naturally and keeps the meaning of high earnings, and both are common words a B2 learner knows.
"Change" fits naturally ("change its processor to a faster model") and is a common A1 word, so a learner could write it and be marked wrong.
"Uncooked" fits with the same meaning, but it is a less common, more formal word for an A2 learner; "fresh" and "rotten" change the meaning.
The closest candidate, "responsibility", is not natural in "product ___ insurance"; "recall" and "safety" are not about legal liability for injuries, so only "liability" fits.
"Service" fits with the meaning bảo dưỡng, but as a verb it is less common at B1; "keep" is awkward without "up to", and "build" changes the meaning.
The closest candidate, "Merry", does not fit because the song sung at birthdays is fixed as 'Happy Birthday'; 'Merry Birthday' and 'Good Birthday' are not natural English.
Only informal or regional variants such as "buddies", "pals" or the British "mates" fit "make new ___", and few A1 learners would write them.
Only less common words such as "briefing" or "catch-up" fit as a meeting; "call" (a phone call) and "practice" (a training session) are natural but change the meaning away from "cuộc họp".
"Payment" fits naturally ("proof of payment" is a very common phrase for a receipt), and a B1 learner knows it, so that learner would be marked wrong.
"Gift" (or "present") fits naturally, as in "buy a cheap gift at the airport, like a keyring or a mug", and is a common A2 word that keeps the sense of quà.

The closest candidates, "puzzle" and "match", do not fit because "board game" is a fixed compound and "play a board puzzle" or "play a board match" is not natural English.
The closest candidate, "timer", can go off but means a countdown timer (hẹn giờ), not a wake-up alarm; "clock" and "reminder" do not naturally go off to wake you up.
"Faculty" could fit ("the chemistry faculty"), but it is a less common, more formal word above B1; "lab" and "class" do not keep the meaning or sound natural.
The closest candidates, 'watch' and 'stream', are natural but mean viewing rather than 'tải xuống', and the clue 'before I leave home' points to saving files for later.
"Hold" (and also "have" or "run") fits naturally in "hold a bake sale" with the meaning tổ chức, and A2 learners commonly know it.
No other common word fits ("list" and "card" sound unnatural here), but the plural "menus" is natural and is missing from accepted_answers.
"Tactics" fits naturally and is close in meaning, but it is a less common B2+ word; "skill" also fits but means "kỹ năng", not "chiến lược".
Only less common words like "occupied" or "swamped" fit with the meaning "bận rộn"; common words like "tired" do not fit naturally with "with my homework" and change the meaning.
The common words "party" and "group" fit naturally ("every party/group with an interest in the company"), and the phrase "with an interest in" already supplies the meaning "bên liên quan".
Only the formal word "surplus" fits naturally with the meaning of lợi nhuận; common words like "gain" or "amount" sound awkward, and "loss" reverses the meaning.
The closest candidate, "relational system", is vague and does not clearly mean "cơ sở dữ liệu"; "model" and "table" do not fit holding millions of migrated records, so only "database" fits.
Only the less common near-synonym "backer" (or "venture capitalist") keeps the meaning; "businessman" is natural but means "doanh nhân", not "nhà đầu tư".

The common B1 word "income" fits naturally ("falling tax income" keeps the meaning of public earnings), and the plural "revenues", which is very common in this phrase, is not among the accepted answers.
Only "application", the full form of "app", fits naturally ("mobile application"); "service" and "website" change the meaning away from "ứng dụng".
The closest candidate, "deficit", means "thâm hụt" rather than "khoản nợ", while "budget" and "loans" either change the meaning or sound unnatural after "national".
Only the rare, technical 'trade' (trade name) also fits; common words like 'company' or 'product' sound unnatural before 'name' here.
The closest candidate, "simmer" ("come to a simmer"), means gentle heating below boiling, not "sôi"; "stop" and "bubble" are not natural with water here, so only "boil" fits.

"Clean" fits naturally ("put the dirty socks in the machine to clean them"), keeps the meaning of giặt, and is a common A1 word.
